correctness.rationale: For any finite lattice with at most one atom, every nonzero element shares the unique atom, so semicomplementation forces its preconditional negation to zero, and identity gives negation of zero equal to one: double-negation inflation holds. If there are distinct atoms p,q, the explicit operation with output 1 on a<=b, q when a=p not<=b, and a meet b otherwise is a T-preconditional. A complete P5 case split on d=a meet b gives the needed bound without distributivity; its negation sends p to q and q to zero, violating F. The unique smallest such carrier is four-element Boolean B2, where P1–P4 and T restrict the entire table to two independently chosen disjoint complement entries (2 x 2), all verified against P5, and F retains the two unmixed choices. Direct checker execution confirmed Boolean T=4,F=2, all 242 labeled ideal lattices on up to four points, an M3 nondistributive instance, and exhaustive small-chain tables. These finite checks corroborate but do not prove the universal finite statement.

originality.rationale: Comparison is about logical implication: the published chain result proves only T=F for linearly ordered finite reducts and gives (n-2)! counts. It does not imply the all-finite-lattice equivalence, universal two-atom witness on nondistributive lattices, or the first four-element branching census. Chen supplies axioms and broad semantics without the atomic criterion in inspected material; Holliday supplies preconditionals and representation, but the identified results do not assert this criterion. Targeted semantic, source, and published-record searches gave no covering theorem. This is best-knowledge originality, not absolute priority proof.

value.rationale: The exact redundancy of an added negation axiom over a fixed algebraic reduct is a structural semantic question, not a restatement of the axiom itself. A one-atom iff test for every finite bounded lattice removes operation-table search, strictly extends the published chain case, and yields a universal one-row perturbation witnessing failure for every two-atom carrier, with a sharp minimal four-element census. The invariant (number of atoms / zero-divisor structure) is intrinsic and naturally motivated by semicomplementation; no new global complexity or representation theorem is asserted.
